children.summary: This section contains the opening remarks for NVIDIA's Q1 2027 Earnings Call. It begins with an introduction by the conference operator, followed by welcome remarks from Toshiya Hari (Vice President-Investor Relations & Strategic Finance). The text outlines the call's agenda, including a question-and-answer session, and provides logistical details regarding the live webcast on NVIDIA's Investor Relations website. It also includes standard legal disclaimers regarding forward-looking statements and references to risk factors found in the company's Forms 10-K and 10-Q.

children.title: Colette M. Kress
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION/Colette M. Kress
children.summary: This page is a transcript from NVIDIA Corp.'s Q1 2027 Earnings Call, featuring remarks by Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress. She reports exceptional financial results, including total revenue of $82 billion and Data Center revenue of $75 billion, driven by strong demand for Blackwell architecture products like the GB300 NVL72. The text also outlines the company's new reporting framework, which divides market platforms into Data Center (Hyperscale and ACIE) and Edge Computing. This page is a transcript from NVIDIA Corp.'s Q1 2027 Earnings Call, focusing on Data Center results and the accelerating demand for AI infrastructure. It details significant revenue growth in hyperscale and ACIE segments, noting that sovereign revenue increased over 80% year-over-year. The text highlights the deployment of Blackwell architecture across major cloud providers like Microsoft, AWS, and Google, and discusses the strategic partnerships with companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. This page is a transcript from NVIDIA Corp.'s Q1 2027 Earnings Call, dated May 20, 2026. It details the company's performance in AI infrastructure, highlighting the success of Blackwell Ultra and the upcoming Vera CPU architecture. The text also covers revenue growth in Edge Computing and Physical AI, mentions partnerships with Google and Uber, and discusses regulatory challenges regarding exports to China.

children.title: Toshiya Hari
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION SECTION/Toshiya Hari
children.summary: This page is a corrected transcript of NVIDIA Corp.'s Q1 2027 Earnings Call dated May 20, 2026. The speaker details financial results including $145 billion in total supply, gross margins around 75%, and record free cash flow of $49 billion. It outlines capital allocation strategies such as increasing the quarterly dividend to $0.20 per share and authorizing an $80 billion share repurchase program. The outlook for Q2 projects revenue of $91 billion, with full-year expectations for 2027 tax rates between 16% and 18%. The section concludes with a transition to the Q&A session led by Toshiya Hari.

children.title: QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION
children.summary: This page is a transcript of the Question and Answer section from NVIDIA Corp.'s Q1 2027 Earnings Call, dated May 20, 2026. It features a question from Joseph Moore of Morgan Stanley regarding business segmentation and competitive differences. Jen Hsun Huang, NVIDIA's CEO, responds by discussing the diversity of AI applications across various industries (such as manufacturing, life sciences, and energy) and environments (from hyperscale clouds to edge devices). He also highlights NVIDIA's unique position in building full-stack technology components.

children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Operator: Your next question comes from Ben Reitzes with Melius Research. Your line is open.

children.title: Ben Reitzes
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Ben Reitzes
children.summary: Ben Reitzes, an analyst from Melius Research LLC, asks Jensen Huang about NVIDIA's growth philosophy. He references the Data Center business's 120% growth ex-China and questions whether the company can grow faster than hyperscaler CapEx, which is forecast to grow 90-100%. He also asks for confirmation on the $3 trillion to $4 trillion data center market size by the end of the decade.

children.title: Jen Hsun Huang
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Jen Hsun Huang
children.summary: This page contains a transcript from the NVIDIA Corp. Q1 2027 Earnings Call, featuring remarks by Jen Hsun Huang. The speaker discusses the segmentation of the Data Center business into two main categories: hyperscalers and AI native clouds (including sovereign AI). He highlights that hyperscaler CapEx is currently at $1 trillion and growing towards $3 to $4 trillion, while the second category involves hundreds of thousands of companies building their own AI factories.

children.title: C.J. Muse
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/C.J. Muse
children.summary: This page is a transcript from the NVIDIA Corp. Q1 2027 Earnings Call held on May 20, 2026. It features a discussion led by analyst C.J. Muse of Cantor Fitzgerald & Co., who asks about NVIDIA's market share in inference and the impact of the Vera Rubin architecture. Jen Hsun Huang responds by highlighting rapid growth in frontier model companies (such as Cursor, Perplexity, TML, Reflection, and Anthropic) and partnerships with cloud providers like Azure, AWS, and CoreWeave. The segment concludes with analyst Timothy Arcuri of UBS Securities LLC asking about traction in custom merchant products like CPX and LPX.

children.title: Timothy Arcuri
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Timothy Arcuri
children.summary: The section titled "Timothy Arcuri" features a question from Timothy Arcuri, an analyst at UBS Securities LLC. He asks about the traction NVIDIA is gaining with custom merchant products like CPX and LPX, specifically referencing a previous comment that SaaS LPX accounts for 20% of the market. He requests further details on this traction and how it fits into the company's broader platform strategy.

children.title: Vivek Arya
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Vivek Arya
children.summary: Vivek Arya, an analyst from Bank of America Securities, asks about the role of CPUs in agentic applications and whether they are cannibalizing GPU workloads. He specifically questions if a previously mentioned $20 billion figure refers to standalone Vera CPUs or is included within the Vera Rubin platform. Jen Hsun Huang responds by clarifying that the $20 billion figure represents standalone CPU sales. He further explains that Vera is utilized in four distinct ways: as part of the Vera Rubin platform (where two Rubins connect to one Vera), as a standalone CPU, with CX9 for storage software stacks, and with CX9 for security and confidential computing.

children.title: Operator: Your next question comes from Jim Schneider with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Operator: Your next question comes from Jim Schneider with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.
children.summary: The Operator introduces the next questioner, Jim Schneider from Goldman Sachs. The section includes his full name and title as an Analyst at Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, followed by his question regarding NVIDIA's $1 trillion revenue visibility, specifically asking about the potential upside from Vera CPUs compared to Rubin and Blackwell platforms, and whether they are considering other product combinations to capture more Total Addressable Market (TAM).

children.title: James Edward Schneider
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/James Edward Schneider
children.summary: James Edward Schneider, an analyst from Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, asks about the potential upside beyond the $1 trillion visibility for Rubin and Blackwell platform revenue discussed at GTC. He specifically inquires if Vera CPUs will be a major source of growth and if NVIDIA is considering other product combinations to capture more Total Addressable Market (TAM). Jen Hsun Huang responds by identifying three drivers for incremental growth: continued share growth in frontier AI models, the inclusion of standalone Vera CPUs which are expected to be the second largest category, and LPX architecture designed for low latency and high interactivity.

children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Operator: Your next question comes from Joshua Buchalter with TD Cowen. Your line is open.

children.title: Joshua Buchalter
children.path: NVDA Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Transcript.pdf/Root/QUESTION AND ANSWER SECTION/Joshua Buchalter
children.summary: Joshua Buchalter, an analyst from TD Cowen, asks Colette M. Kress about the ramp-up of the Vera Rubin architecture compared to the GB300 benchmark. He questions whether the new silicon will result in a similar slope or a more gradual ramp. Colette M. Kress responds that Vera Rubin is scheduled for launch in the second half of the year, starting in Q3 and continuing into Q4 and Q1 of the next year, noting that demand is already planned with major customers ready.
